harness: heuristics-ab.ts first version (UNPAIRED: different seed per seat order)
rationale: Harness smoke test with identical strategies on both seats. The 35/65 split measured the on-draw seat advantage, not strategy strength, and exposed that per-seat-order seeds break pairing. The harness was rebuilt to the paired design (one seed per pairing, both seat orders) and this run is superseded by the paired null calibration.

harness: heuristics-ab.ts (paired seeds, 45 authored-botlab pairings x 4 match seeds x 2 seat orders)
rationale: Identical strategies on both seats: this is the metric noise floor. Paired improvement must clear roughly +/-0.04 at 180 pairs (about +/-0.022 at 540 pairs) to be trusted.
Free-steal mandate (steal-only prompt when the rival has no ready blocker; 0-power units never steal). Weak positive at 360; extended for significance.
Removal mandate (weakest-sufficient attacker per defender; combat outranks developing) plus weakest-winner selection.
Breakpoint/top-safe bonus 60, stacking penalty -10 per attached gear. No signal; penalty strengthened to -10 - 12x stacked before the next round.
Plain-power gears never attach to face-up non-GO-SOLO legends. Rarely fires (authored profiles manage hosts) but is a rules-correctness fix the user requested; neutral on the bench.

+5.3 percent raw win rate, about 5 sigma at 540 pairs. The single biggest individual contributor: blocking negates a steal even when the blocker dies, so a steal is only safe when no ready blocker exists - and then it is strictly +EV.
Individually inside the noise band. Kept because the combined-set run (below) shows strong positive interaction - the marginal runs under-measure contribution.
Exactly null individually even after retune. Kept for the same interaction reason as remove-targets.

Combined effect is roughly twice the sum of individual marginals (+0.14): strong positive interaction between the removal and steal mandates (double-attack combat turns). The shipped configuration is exactly what this run validated.

armA.heuristics: all on + authored curve lines narrow before combat policies

rationale: Fix attempt for two curve-prompt-lines failures: letting authored curve lines narrow before the combat mandates hands the curve window back full control and costs 25 points of paired improvement. Combat overriding authored lines in the window is winning games.

The mandates' value comes precisely from forcing attacks the search would decline; keeping pass as a candidate gives the search an exit and loses the gain. Curve vetoes are instead handled by the empty-set pass fallback in decide().

Statistically equivalent to the +0.2074 original while passing every test (curve-prompt-lines 33/33, engine automation 210/210). Committed as 4c6016488e. The empty-set fallback passes instead of re-rolling through greedy, so curve vetoes hold without softening the mandates.
Masterful (ability-aware) is not stronger than Sharp in mirror play over the authored bot-lab pool.
Bots must play: repeatedState is a hard bug, not a tradeoff. Depth-4 lines revisit public boards. Reliability beats the inconclusive win-rate bump.

armA.heuristics: all on + blocker choice left to the search

rationale: Greedy blocker thresholds (urgency, deny-steal bar, chump valuation, preserve-for-later) already match search quality. The experiment also changed modeled-opponent blocking and broke two numerical-pressure tests. Gate removed.

Every one of the 360 games is identical to the deny-steal run of the same size: the pessimism offset only seeds minimax values that real lines always dominate, so it cannot flip decisions. Knob added then removed (dead code).

Authored deck profiles already resolve blockDirectStealsAtLeast to 1, so the override was a no-op. Both this and the pessimism run produced byte-identical games to each other, which is how the inertness was detected.
Exactly zero at 180 pairs with no failures: depth-3 search breadth is saturated. More nodes find nothing the smaller budget misses.
